original_question: Let L be a finite field of characteristic p with |L| > 2, and let s be an invertible exponent, meaning gcd(s, |L|-1) = 1, for the power permutation x -> x^s on L. If s is congruent to 1 modulo p - 1, must the exponent be singular, that is, must there exist some a in L^x such that the Weil sum W_{L,s}(a) = sum_{x in L} mu(x^s - ax) is equal to 0?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 (Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture, 1976) in Section 1. Your draft is aiming at the full vanishing conjecture itself, not the narrower adjacent Problem 1.2, which asks only for a proof in the special cases q=2^k or q=3^k without elliptic-curve methods. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper-faithful formulation: it works over a finite field of characteristic p, includes the condition q=|L|>2, requires gcd(s,q-1)=1 so that x -> x^s is a power permutation, uses the congruence s ≡ 1 mod (p-1), and asks whether there exists a nonzero a with W_{L,s}(a)=0, which is exactly the paper’s notion of a singular exponent. That matches the content of Conjecture 1.1 essentially exactly. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
missing_details: The paper defines μ to be the canonical additive character of the finite field; your draft writes μ but does not specify that it is the canonical additive character. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))

The paper treats s as an integer exponent (equivalently, modulo q-1), so a fully stand-alone version should say explicitly that s is a positive integer with gcd(s,q-1)=1, where q=|L|. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))

To be fully paper-faithful, the definition of singular should be tied explicitly to the power permutation x -> x^s over L: s is singular over L if there exists a in L^× such that W_{L,s}(a)=0. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
refined_question: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p and order q>2, let μ be the canonical additive character of F, and let s be a positive integer with gcd(s,q-1)=1. For a in F, define the Weil sum W_{F,s}(a)=sum_{x in F} μ(x^s-ax). Say that the power permutation x -> x^s (equivalently, the exponent s) is singular over F if there exists a in F^× such that W_{F,s}(a)=0. Must every invertible exponent s satisfying s ≡ 1 mod (p-1) be singular over F? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, under the same hypotheses q=|F|>2, gcd(s,q-1)=1, and s ≡ 1 mod (p-1), if μ is the canonical additive character of F, must the q x q matrix M=((μ((x-y)^s)))_{x,y in F} have rank strictly less than q-1? The paper states this as the restated form of the vanishing conjecture in Conjecture 2.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
justification: Section 1 defines the Fourier coefficient/Weil sum for power maps, defines an invertible exponent as one with gcd(s,q-1)=1, and defines singularity by the existence of a nonzero a with vanishing Weil sum; immediately after that, Conjecture 1.1 states the vanishing conjecture in exactly the form your draft is trying to express. The nearby Problem 1.2 is only a special-case challenge for q=2^k or 3^k, so it is not the right target for your draft. Section 2 then explicitly says Conjecture 1.1 is equivalent to the matrix-rank statement recorded as Conjecture 2.3. Also, in the inspected arXiv/journal version, the neighboring labels are Problem 1.2 and Remark 1.3 rather than Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/abs/1412.8530))
